annotation.title_clean: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.title_en: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kovacic, M.; Marvin, S.; While, A.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how California municipalities regulate sidewalk delivery robots, using policy analysis and interviews. It identifies prohibitive, permissive and collaborative regulatory approaches, showing that first-mover firms such as Starship shaped permitting, liability and insurance rules.
key_provisions_or_claims: California cities have used prohibitive, permissive and collaborative sidewalk regulation for delivery robots.
First-mover firms like Starship strongly shaped municipal and state permitting rules.
Palo Alto requires encroachment permits, operator liability, $2–4M insurance and 24-hour incident reporting.
Urban robots are disruptive because they challenge existing regulatory frameworks and human–machine conventions.
Campus and precinct trials act as single-company testbeds with bespoke regulatory environments.
